elements.name: straight bushing
elements.note: Same 0.1875 in nominal as the tan-link bushing but a DIFFERENT tolerance band (4.71/4.81 vs 4.63/4.76) -- a different part, for the .250 in bolt.

source_ref.note: NAS77A4-015 is ABSENT from the 217755 parts list. The as-drawn bushing at this joint is Joby 214943-002 (BUSHING, PLAIN, ALUMINUM BRONZE, .250" ID), balloon 28 in DETAIL X. DECIDED 2026-08-13 (handoff spec_pile_gap_join), on the merits and with the value UNCHANGED at 4.762 / 4.71 / 4.81 mm: NAS77 IS in `data/inbox/specs/` -- `JB_NAS77.pdf` and the NAS77 page of both RBC plain-bearing catalogues (printed p92 in the 2016 reprint, p98 in the 2008 web edition, of which `JB_NAS77.pdf` is a one-page extract) -- and reading it does not source this element, it rules the part number out. NAS77 is the UNLINED FLANGED series (the straight/plain one is NAS76, the page before it in each) and the as-drawn part is a plain bushing; the dash decode printed on the NAS77 page is "Length in .010 increments (ex: -025 = .25 in.)", which makes NAS77A4-015 .150 in long against the .1875 in this element folds; and the length tolerance printed there is L +/-.005 in, not the +/-.002 in that 4.71/4.81 mm implies. (For contrast, NAS76 decodes its dash as 32nds of an inch and controls length +.000/-.005 -- a different rule and a different band, so neither series supports the modelled numbers.) The element therefore stays `kind: workbook` / `untraced` and stays on the gap list. 214943-002's part drawing is still the document that closes it, and it is still not in the pile.

No bearing balloon in DETAIL X -- internal to 208510-007 VARIABLE PITCH ACTUATOR ASSEMBLY (balloon 1). The workbook's comment column names MS21299C4K on this row, but that part is a countersunk washer (see column_I_caveat). CANDIDATE IDENTITY, RECORDED NOT CLAIMED (2026-09-15, handoff stack_fable_audit): the modelled band 8.66/8.71 mm equals the RBC catalog's MS14101-4 ball width (.343 in, +.000/-.002 -- the NARROW series' .250-bore row, PDF page 21 of RBC_Aerospace_Plain_Bearings_Web.pdf) to the digit. A value matching is not a feature matching (SOP trap 11), no parts list this repo can read names the VPA rod end's bearing, and the VPA is not one of the two link types Jeff's 2026-09-15 note assigned bearings to -- so the element stays `kind: workbook` / `untraced`, and confirming the rod-end bearing part number is on the operator queue. If it IS MS14101-4, this element becomes re-citable exactly the way the tan-link bearing was.

export.note: Established 2026-09-16 by handoff citation_identity_correctness, which re-cited this value from the PRELIM 215197 fixture to the RELEASED plate. 215735-A is copied into this repo's own inbox (data/inbox/drawings/PROVENANCE.md, 'Copied 2026-09-16'), sha256 verified identical on both sides. Both drawing-checker runs of it -- 20260813_180734_215735-A and 20260819_153213_215735-A -- record this same sha256 in their run_meta.json inputs, and no other 215735 PDF exists in drawing-checker's inbox or fixtures, so 'which export' has a unique answer here. This element's own note, unlike its tan_link sibling's, does not record a session reading this address on 215735-A for the value -- the value was read on 215197 and carried across because the callout at this address is unchanged; the basis here is that unchanged address plus uniqueness of the export, not a written record of a fresh reading.

source_ref.note: WHICH feature is still ambiguous, and 215735-A widens it rather than settling it. 215197 A.1 carried TWO 4.06 ±0.10 callouts: '5X 4.06 ±0.10' at sheet 2 zone D10 (⊥0.05 G, 5X INDIVIDUALLY) and a single '4.06 ±0.10' at sheet 1 zone D5 (⌖0.2 A B C, datum D). On 215735-A, measured 2026-09-16, there are THREE: the same 5X group at sheet 2 zone D10, the sheet 1 zone D5 one, AND a second sheet 1 callout at zone D6 -- 215197 printed 8.80 ±0.10 in that position, so the released plate has a further feature that came to 4.06. The workbook's 3.96/4.16 matches all three. This joint is qty 1, which still argues for a sheet-1 callout rather than the 5X group; the tolerance alone still cannot decide, and there are now two sheet-1 candidates rather than one. The citation stays on the address it has always named -- sheet 2 zone D10 -- because re-pointing it at a different printed callout is a value-identity decision, not a currency one, and nothing in the released drawing decides it. Separately, DETAIL X balloons the VPA (1) against the TANGENTIAL LINK MOUNT 215175-002 (72), not the pitch plate 215177-001 -- so the pitch plate may be the wrong part entirely for this flange, a doubt the re-cite from 215197 to 215735 does not touch.

elements.note: 0.812 +/-0.010 in. Workbook row 71 restates the grip with no tolerance; row 73 is the toleranced one and is the row used. RE-CITED 2026-08-06 (handoff traced_labels_and_ratio): the band now comes off the NAS6404 standard, not the parts list.

source_ref.note: One sheet covers NAS6403 through NAS6420: the 'Grip ±.010' column is shared by every basic number, and the per-basic-number columns to its right give overall LENGTH ±.015 (NAS6404 = .2500-28, the .250-28 thread this joint uses; its dash-13 length is 1.182). Sheet 2 CODE block decodes the part number -- dash 13 x .0625 = .8125 -> .812 as printed, 'U' = unplated, 'D' = drilled shank -- and its EXAMPLE OF PART NUMBER block is written against NAS6404 specifically. Sheet 2 note (a) defines grip as underside of head to the end of the full cylindrical shank. WAS `kind: parts_list` / `confidence: traced` citing 217755 balloon 27, whose own note admitted 'the +/-.010 in is untraced (NAS6404 spec absent)'. Which bolt sits in this joint is still the parts list's evidence: NAS6404U13D, find 27 qty 1, ballooned in 217755 sheet 5 DETAIL X. paths.label: total stack under the fastener grip

checks.label: worst case (MMC+ = max shank out)
checks.guidance: Grip minus the clamped stack. Negative at minimum means the thread run-out is pulled inside the joint; positive at maximum means full-diameter shank protrudes past the nut face. This stack has NO thread-transition allowance, unlike the tan-link take 1.

notes: The as-drawn joint is a castellated nut (MS9363-10, balloon 25) + cotter pin (MS24665-229, balloon 26). Grip length alone cannot answer this joint: the binding constraint is whether a castellation slot lines up with the cotter hole. The workbook does not model it; neither does this transcription.
This stack has no thread-transition element and no second washer branch, so it has strictly less modelling than the tan-link take 1.
